title: Applied ML: Regression Triage and Quantization Playbook
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the standard process for detecting, triaging, and remediating quality regressions for models served by Redwood Inference, with a special focus on regressions introduced by quantization and inference-time configuration changes. It integrates signals from the eval harness, production telemetry, prompt set benchmarks, and customer reports into a single reproducible workflow that guides engineers through diagnosis, mitigation, and long-term prevention.

Scope:
- Applies to all model onboarding, model variant rollouts (quantized and non-quantized), and continuous evaluation pipelines owned by Applied ML and Serving Runtime teams.
- Covers detection signals, severity classification, immediate remediation steps, deeper debugging workflows, and postmortem actions.
- Does NOT replace security incident response or privacy breach processes (see security-and-compliance).

Goals:
1) Detect regressions quickly with high precision and minimal noise.
2) Provide a reproducible, cross-team triage workflow that minimizes MTTR.
3) Categorize and remediate quantization-specific failures without unnecessary rollback when safe mitigations exist.
4) Feed learnings back to model onboarding, eval harness artifacts, and quantization profile libraries.

Ownership and Roles:
- Primary owner: Applied ML (onboarding + eval harness)
- Secondary owner: Eng - Serving Runtime (quantization, runtime kernels)
- Incident lead: Assigned on call ML engineer (pager rota)
- Stakeholders: Product, SRE, Customer Success (for escalations)

Key Definitions (use consistently):
- Regression: statistically significant negative change in one or more eval metrics or user-facing quality signals compared to the pinned baseline.
- Regression window: rolling 24-72 hour window for production metric changes; configurable per-model.
- Quantization profile: configuration set (precision, operator fallback, per-channel scaling) used to compile a model variant.

Signal sources (ordered by priority):
1) Eval harness automated alerts: A/B eval runs that compare candidate variant vs. pinned baseline across official prompt sets and metrics (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, intent precision/recall, hallucination rate).
2) Production telemetry: token-level perplexity drift, increased rerate/abandonment, soft-metrics from application (e.g., classification accuracy, action success rate).
3) Customer-reported quality regressions (support tickets, SRE escalations).
4) Canary / rollout: increased error/latency or degraded qualitative samples in canary cohorts.

Severity matrix (triage quick reference):
- Sev P0 (Critical): High-impact production regression affecting >=5% of traffic or causing major customer bugs (data loss, misclassification with safety impact). Immediate rollback required.
- Sev P1 (High): Significant quality drop on core prompt sets or business metrics for key customers (>=1% traffic) - mitigation within 2 hours; rollback if mitigation fails.
- Sev P2 (Moderate): Model-specific metric degradation in eval harness that does not yet impact production; schedule hotfix or retrain within 3 business days.
- Sev P3 (Low): Minor metric drift or a single prompt failure; schedule investigation during next sprint.

Triage workflow (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Alert generated by eval harness or monitoring dashboard. The alert must include the failing prompt set, metrics and the candidate vs baseline diff, sample responses, and the quantization profile (if applicable).
2) Triage kickoff (15 min): Incident lead picks up alert, verifies signal (re-run failing eval locally if possible), classifies severity, and notifies stakeholders via Slack channel #applied-ml-triage.
3) Initial mitigation (first 30-60 min):
   - For P0/P1: immediate rollback to pinned baseline variant (use serving control-plane change) unless a safe hotfix exists (see Mitigation options).
   - For P2/P3: create a triage ticket with all artifacts and assign to an ML engineer.
4) Deep diagnosis (within 4 hours for P0/P1, 48 hours for P2):
   - Reproduce the failure in the eval harness with the exact runtime config and tokenizer. Use the same seed and batch shapes where possible.
   - Run a diff across prompt groups to localize failure surface (semantic, safety, numeric instability).
   - If quantization involved, run the candidate model at FP16/FP32 to confirm whether the regression is quantization-induced.
5) Fix & validate:
   - If quantization bug: try per-operator fallback or modified quantization params (see Quantization-specific procedures). Re-run full prompt sets and production-like sampling.
   - If model defect: escalate to Model Onboarding owner for retrain or nudge with targeted fine-tune.
6) Roll forward: After validation, promote patch candidate through canary and staged rollout with increased monitoring.
7) Postmortem and preventive actions: Document root cause, corrective steps, and update the relevant quantization profile/eval prompt sets. Add regression test(s) to the eval harness if missing.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by safety and speed):
- Rollback to pinned baseline model variant (fastest, safest).
- Switch to FP16 or software fallback for specific operators (if runtime supports dynamic operator overrides).
- Route traffic to a Dedicated pool or different region if degradation is localized to hardware/kernel.
- Apply conservative decoding config changes (reduce temperature, enforce deterministic sampling) to limit hallucinations temporarily.

Required artifacts for reproducible triage (attach to ticket):
- Eval harness run ID and diff report (CSV/JSON OK).
- Sample prompt set and 10 representative responses (candidate + baseline).
- Serving config: model id, variant id, quantization profile name, runtime flags, tokenizer version.
- Production trace ids (if available) and relevant logs.
- Canary cohort IDs and percentages.

Quantization-specific procedures:
1) Repro check: run candidate variant under full-precision (FP32/FP16) and compare metric deltas. If delta disappears in FP32/FP16, classify as quantization-induced.
2) Narrow scope: binary search quantized operators by selectively enabling FP fallback for suspect operator groups (attention, layernorm, softmax).
3) Profile and inspect weight activations: look for large outliers or dynamic range shifts that cause quantization clipping.
4) Try alternative per-channel scales or symmetric vs asymmetric quantization in the quantization profile.
5) If instability persists, create a new quantization profile and mark as experimental; add to the quantization-profiles library with metadata about the vulnerability.

Quantization profile template (example, add to repo as YAML):
- profile_name: "int8-safe-2026-12"
- precision: "int8"
- scheme: "per-channel-symmetric"
- fallback_ops: ["layernorm", "softmax"]
- calibration_dataset: "prompt-set-core-v2"
- notes: "Conservative per-channel symmetric scaling; falls back layernorm and softmax to FP16"

Model onboarding checklist (must be completed before production pin):
1) Eval harness coverage: full prompt set pass at target thresholds for core metrics and no individual prompt regressions beyond tolerance.
2) Quantization tests: run FP32->FP16->int8 profiles and ensure no metric drop above defined thresholds.
3) Load & latency tests: service under expected QPS with P95 latency targets met.
4) Safety and guardrails: run safety prompt sets and enforce failure thresholds.
5) CI gating: add model variant to gating pipeline that replays critical prompt sets on every change to quantization profiles or runtime kernels.

Prompt sets & benchmark integration:
- All prompt sets used for deployment must be versioned and stored in prompt-sets repo with metadata: owner, intent, expected metric bounds, last-run hash.
- When new regressions are discovered, add negative examples to a focused regression prompt set so future runs fail fast.
- Maintain a lightweight smoke prompt set for canary validation (<=100 prompts) and a comprehensive set for nightly full-eval.

Monitoring, dashboards and SLOs (examples):
- Eval harness nightly job: runs full benchmark at 02:00 UTC, triggers alert on metric drop > 2x the configured sigma.
- Production drift alert: token perplexity drift > 5% over 24h or customer-facing errors up 10% over baseline triggers P1.
- Canary gating: 1% of traffic for 1 hour with automated human review if any semantic regressions occur.

Example alert config (prometheus-style pseudo YAML):
- alert: ModelPerplexityDrift
  expr: (avg_over_time(model_token_perplexity[24h]) - baseline_perplexity) / baseline_perplexity > 0.05
  for: 30m
  labels: { severity: "P1" }
  annotations: { runbook: "/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-evals-regression-triage-and-quantization-playbook-2026-12-15" }

CI gating and eval harness best practices:
- Gate quantization profile changes behind a matrix of evals: smoke, core prompts, safety, latency.
- Keep eval runs deterministic: fix RNG seeds, tokenizers, and sampling configs for regression test runs.
- Store eval outputs and diffs in the artifact store with run metadata for 90 days.

Post-incident actions (to be completed within 5 business days for P0/P1):
- Full postmortem with owners, timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups.
- Update quantization-profiles library (add safe profile or mark profile as deprecated).
- Add regression prompt(s) to regression suite.
- Schedule knowledge transfer session for on-call and stakeholders if changes to process or tools are made.

Appendix: Helpful CLI snippets and checks
- Re-run eval harness locally: ./eval-harness/run.py --run-id <id> --output artifacts/<id>
- Compare baseline vs candidate: python tools/eval_diff.py --baseline artifacts/baseline.json --candidate artifacts/candidate.json --metrics perplexity,safety_score
- Promote rollback via control plane: rcli model promote --model-id <baseline> --env production

Related documents:
- applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025 (eval harness run standards)
- quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026 (detailed quantization guidance)

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: @priya.natarajan (Applied ML)
- Secondary: @runtime-oncall (Serving Runtime)
- Pager: #oncall-applied-ml (for P0)

This playbook is reviewed quarterly and after every P0/P1 regression. Any updates must be noted in the change log section of the page.
